symbols.description: Organization cited as stating the percentages of congestion attributed to bottlenecks and poor signal timing.
symbols.name: FHWA

symbols.description: Traffic condition discussed as having recurring and nonrecurring causes.
symbols.name: congestion

symbols.description: Localized point or condition of traffic congestion associated with queues upstream and free-flowing traffic downstream.
symbols.name: bottleneck

symbols.description: Signal-timing condition identified as a cause of congestion.
symbols.name: poor signal timing

symbols.description: Congestion category associated with bottlenecks and poor signal timing and described as existing regularly.
symbols.name: recurring congestion

symbols.description: Congestion category consisting of congestion other than recurring congestion, including congestion associated with special events, bad weather, work zones, and traffic incidents.
symbols.name: nonrecurring congestion

symbols.description: Study cited as the primary basis for the quoted congestion attribution, undertaken mostly for or using data mostly from the I-95 Corridor Coalition.
symbols.name: congestion study

symbols.description: Coalition associated with the congestion study and its data.
symbols.name: I-95 Corridor Coalition

symbols.description: Indicators that the cited study reportedly did not break out, identify, or stratify.
symbols.name: congestion indicators

symbols.description: Event identified as an example of a nonrecurring congestion cause.
symbols.name: special event

symbols.description: Weather condition identified as an example of a nonrecurring congestion cause.
symbols.name: bad weather

symbols.description: Roadway work condition identified as an example of a nonrecurring congestion cause.
symbols.name: work zone

symbols.description: Incident identified as an example of a nonrecurring congestion cause.
symbols.name: traffic incident

symbols.description: Definition of a bottleneck, for which the literature is described as having little consensus.
symbols.name: bottleneck definition

symbols.description: Line of traffic formed upstream of a bottleneck.
symbols.name: queue

symbols.description: Direction or location relative to a bottleneck where queues form and traffic may propagate.
symbols.name: upstream

symbols.description: Direction or location relative to a bottleneck associated with free-flowing traffic or a bottleneck front.
symbols.name: downstream

symbols.description: Theory cited as categorizing traffic into three phases.
symbols.name: Kerner's traffic theory

symbols.description: Traffic phase or unrestricted traffic condition in Kerner's categorization.
symbols.name: free-flow

symbols.description: Traffic phase described as localized congestion and associated with a fixed downstream front.
symbols.name: synchronized flow

symbols.description: Traffic phase described as systemic congestion in which downstream traffic velocity moves while traffic may propagate upstream through bottlenecks.
symbols.name: wide-moving jam

symbols.description: Front at which Kerner's synchronized traffic is fixed and which is described as a de facto bottleneck.
symbols.name: downstream front

symbols.description: Velocity of downstream traffic discussed in relation to wide-moving jams.
symbols.name: traffic velocity

symbols.description: Demand for roadway use that can overwhelm available roadway capacity.
symbols.name: traffic demand

symbols.description: Available capacity of a roadway that can be overwhelmed by traffic demand.
symbols.name: roadway capacity

symbols.description: Roadway context in which many cars may try to travel at the same time.
symbols.name: highway

symbols.description: Roadway extent used to distinguish localized bottleneck congestion from congestion pervasive along an entire corridor.
symbols.name: corridor

symbols.description: Physical or operational roadway condition that can produce a bottleneck when traffic demand overwhelms capacity.
symbols.name: physical bottleneck cause

symbols.description: Example of a physical bottleneck cause involving a roadway lane reduction.
symbols.name: lane drop

symbols.description: Roadway design deficiency identified as a physical bottleneck cause.
symbols.name: operationally deficient roadway design

symbols.description: Roadway traffic condition given as an example of a bottleneck cause.
symbols.name: weaving condition

symbols.description: Condition given as an example of a bottleneck cause.
symbols.name: sun glare

symbols.description: Traffic behavior given as an example of a bottleneck cause.
symbols.name: rubbernecking

symbols.description: Roadway feature given as an example of a bottleneck cause.
symbols.name: vertical climb

symbols.description: Traffic delay that occurs when a recurring bottleneck's design deficiency combines with traffic overburden, or when traffic is caused by a nonrecurring event.
symbols.name: delay

symbols.description: Traffic demand exceeding or overloading the available roadway design or capacity in the context of a recurring bottleneck.
symbols.name: traffic overburden

symbols.description: Design of the roadway that may contain a deficiency and otherwise operate safely and unobtrusively.
symbols.name: roadway design

symbols.description: Vehicles and their movement on roadways, categorized by Kerner into traffic phases.
symbols.name: traffic

symbols.description: Congestion confined to a local area, exemplified by synchronized flow and traffic bottlenecks.
symbols.name: localized congestion

symbols.description: Congestion described as more or less systemic in relation to wide-moving jams.
symbols.name: systemic congestion

symbols.description: Narrow route sense of the dictionary definition of a bottleneck.
symbols.name: roadway route
